title: Does `.all()` in Django re-query the Database or use the cache?
q_body: I am getting very conflicting messages. From Django Queryset docs, I am reading ( https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/5.1/ref/models/querysets/#django.db.models.query.QuerySet.all ): When a QuerySet is evaluated, it typically caches its results. If the data in the database might have changed since a QuerySet was evaluated, you can get updated results for the same query by calling all() on a previously evaluated QuerySet. But then under the prefetch_related section, it shows that using .all() on the sub-objects uses results from the cache: >>> restaurants = Restaurant.objects.prefetch_related( ... Prefetch("pizzas", queryset=queryset), ... ) >>> vegetarian_pizzas = restaurants[0].pizzas.all() Here, apparently vegetarian_pizzas doesn't trigger a database query. So...which is it - what does all() actually do? Why does it trigger a database query on the outer but then not for sub-objects? I'm confused.

title: How can I make all attributes in a Python dataclass optional without rewriting each one?
q_body: I have this data class: @dataclass class User: id: str name: str pwd: str picture: str url: str age: int # many, many more attributes Now, I have to make all of the attributes of my data class optional because of a change in the data I am receiving. I know I can do something like this: @dataclass class User: id: Optional[str] = None name: Optional[str] = None # and so on for the 25-30 attributes I have But is there a more efficient way to accomplish this without having to manually write Optional[..] = None for every line? For example, I used to get data like: attributes = {"id": "18ut2", "pwd": "qwerty", "name": "John Doe", "picture": None, "age": None, "url": "www.example.com"} user = User(**attributes) Before, if the attribute was None , the key was not omitted. Unlike now, when a key is None , the entire key is omitted. Example of current data: attributes = {"id": "18ut2", "pwd": "qwerty", "name": "John Doe", "url": "www.example.com"} # No picture or age key anymore user = User(**attributes) # Now throws an error Error: TypeError: User.__init__() missing 2 required positional arguments: 'picture' and 'age' Note: I know overriding __init__ or using __init_subclass__ , but those come with limitations, so I am looking for a solution that avoids that.
